uncited: This method encodes the attributes of a sparse voxel octree by storing deltas relative to the attributes of neighboring voxels, rather than storing absolute values or parent-relative deltas.
It solves the problem of high memory bandwidth and storage costs for dense attribute data (e.g., color, normals) in sparse representations by exploiting spatial coherence.

Unlike its sibling [Sparse Voxel Octree Structure Encoding/Decoding](3012-sparse-voxel-octree-structure-encoding-decoding.md) which handles topology, or [Sparse Voxel Octree Attribute Encoding (Parent)](9709-sparse-voxel-octree-attribute-encoding-parent.md) which uses the parent node, this method uses immediate spatial neighbors to predict the current voxel's attribute.
- `attr`: An $[N, C]$ tensor containing the original attribute values for each voxel, where $C$ is the number of attribute channels.
The method assumes a global grid of resolution `res`.
Voxels are identified by their integer coordinates $(x, y, z)$.
The "neighbors" are typically defined as the 6-connected (face-sharing) or 26-connected (edge/corner-sharing) neighbors within the grid.
For implementation, a hash map or a dense grid buffer (if memory permits) is used to look up the attribute of a neighbor given its coordinate.
**Neighbor Lookup:** For each voxel $i$ at coordinate $p_i = (x_i, y_i, z_i)$, identify its set of existing neighbors $\mathcal{N}_i$.
A neighbor $j$ exists if $p_j$ is in the set of active voxel coordinates and $p_j$ is adjacent to $p_i$ (e.g., $|x_i - x_j| + |y_i - y_j| + |z_i - z_j| = 1$ for face neighbors).
**Prediction:** Select a reference neighbor $j^* \in \mathcal{N}_i$.
If no neighbors exist, the prediction is zero.
where $\text{attr}_i$ is the $C$-dimensional attribute vector of voxel $i$.
**Output:** Store $\delta_i$ in the output tensor.
- **Boundary Voxels:** Voxels on the edge of the grid may have fewer than 6 neighbors.
The method must handle missing neighbors gracefully (e.g., by skipping them or using a default prediction of 0).
- **No Neighbors:** If a voxel has no active neighbors, the delta is simply the attribute value itself (assuming a zero prediction).
- **Precision:** The delta values should be quantized or stored in a format suitable for compression, as they are expected to be small if spatial coherence is high.
Decodes the attribute of a sparse voxel octree from its parent node and its deltas.
It uses the parent node's attribute as the prediction source instead of spatial neighbors.
This is useful when the octree structure is explicitly available and parent-child relationships are well-defined.
It is chosen when the octree hierarchy is deep and parent-child coherence is stronger than spatial neighbor coherence.
- **Time Complexity:** $O(N \cdot k)$ where $N$ is the number of voxels and $k$ is the number of neighbors checked (typically 6 or 26).
Neighbor lookup is $O(1)$ with a hash map or $O(\log N)$ with a tree.
- **Memory Complexity:** $O(N \cdot C)$ for storing the deltas.
Can achieve better compression ratios than parent-based encoding if the octree is shallow or irregular.
Boundary conditions must be handled carefully.
- **When to use:** When spatial coherence is high and the octree structure is not strictly hierarchical or when parent-child relationships are not the primary source of redundancy.
This method is part of the [o-voxel-gpu](https://github.com/quantaji/o-voxel-gpu) library, which provides efficient GPU-accelerated operations for sparse voxel octrees.
It is designed for real-time rendering and compression of 3D data.
